thread:
kat: Heads-up — customer `acme-vpc` on private has a weird failover case. Their on-prem egress to control plane was blocked by a firewall rule and the control plane routed inference to our hosted pool in us-west. Customer flagged telemetry/data residency concerns.

raj: Oof. Do we have a clear invariant that private deployments can never egress model payloads to hosted by default? I thought we prefer local model variants.

olivia: We do in intent, but current smart-routing policy uses a region+capacity fallback that doesn't check "egress_allowed" before rerouting. So when their ip was unreachable, it considered hosted as higher-priority.

kat: Exact issue. They have strict allowed_regions + egress_restrictions. The decision logic should prefer "compatible_local_variant" over cross-region hosted endpoints when egress blocked.

ellen: Agree. Two asks: (1) policy change so control_plane respects per-tenant egress flag before fallback, (2) console UX to make this explicit in rollout pages (checkbox: "allow hosted fallback on egress failure").

raj: Proposed minimal change (pseudo-config):

```
routing_policy:
  tier: private
  allowed_egress: false
  fallback_order:
    - local_quantized_variant
    - local_fp16_variant
    - hosted (only if allowed_egress == true)
```

raj: That prevents hosted fallback unless tenant explicitly opts-in.

olivia: Nice. Also need telemetry: create a dashboard and alerts that trigger when fallback_to_hosted occurs for private tenants. Otherwise ops won't notice. Suggest fields on telemetry event: tenant_id, reason (egress_block|capacity), chosen_variant, attempted_region.

cs-ops: +1 on telemetry. We had a ticket from the customer about PII possibly leaving their VPC. If we emit an event with tenant_id masked and a severity score, we can route to security without leaking payloads.

kat: For console UX, add a small banner on Private deployment page: "Hosted fallback currently disabled for this tenant" (or show a toggle). The rollout modal should show explicit consequences: latency, cost, and egress risk.

ellen: Also we should codify a backwards-compatible rollout: default keep existing behavior, but ship opt-in enforcement for new tenants and a migration tool for existing ones. Put an experimental feature flag first.

infra-bot: deploy-checker: canary job started for change set "private-routing-egress-guard" on eng-platform/canary, 3 tests queued.

raj: Implementation notes: control-plane router has two decision points — "route selection" and "egress-resolve". Move the egress_allowed check to the top of route selection so hosted endpoints are filtered out early. Also add a small cache TTL for tenant egress status to avoid extra RPCs per request.

olivia: On telemetry schema: event name `private_routing_fallback` with tags: [tenant_env, fallback_target, egress_flag, model_variant]. Keep payload minimal (no prompt/response).

kat: Who wants to own the console copy and rollout messaging? I can draft the banner + modal copy if someone else wires the toggle.

ellen: I’ll take the migration plan doc and add checklist for CS communication. cs-ops — can you draft the customer-safe incident blurb in case any other tenants see fallback?

cs-ops: Yep. Will prepare short blurb and escalation play. Also will coordinate on opt-in emails for tenants who previously relied on hosted fallback.

raj: I'll push a small PR with the policy filter and unit tests. Will wait for canary results then we flip feature flag.

kat: Sounds good. If infra-bot can report canary pass here we merge and schedule console work next sprint. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
